newsitem.title: USA: Calif agriculture output reached $24.5 bln in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Calif agriculture output reached $24.5 bln in 1996.

text.p: California said on Wednesday its agricultural output totaled $24.5 billion in 1996, an all-time high for the state.
The 1996 production and income total represented a $1.1 billion increase from 1995's output of $23.4 billion, Gov. Pete Wilson announced at a press conference in Sacramento.

"California's growers and harvesters continue to set higher standards and reap even greater rewards for the remarkable job they do in managing the land and catering to the world's needs," Wilson said.
California has been the nation's top agriculture producer for 50 consecutive years, Wilson said.

In 1996, California's agricultural production and income was nearly double that of Texas, and almost exceeded the combined totals of the next three leading states -- Iowa, Nebraska and Illinois, the governor said.

Ten food and agricultural products in California reached billion dollar values in 1996, including milk and cream at $3.7 billion, grapes at $2.2 billion, nursery products at $1.6 billion, cattle and calves at $1.2 billion, cotton lint at $1.1 billion and almonds at $1 billion.
These were followed by hay, lettuce, flowers and foliage, and processing tomatoes.
Fresno, Tulare, Kern, Monterey, Merced, San Joaquin, Stanislaus, Riverside and San Diego were the top agriculture producing counties.
